headline: 15 commitments on Bengaluru's register: the city's climate plan joins it with dated water targets - 3 delivered (ward-level consumption data is now public), 6 on track on their owners' own numbers, and 6 overdue, stalled or unverifiable.
intro: Dated commitments by the institutions that manage this city's water - BWSSB, BDA, the Karnataka government and the tribunals that set deadlines for them - made to residents, courts and funders, and followed from announcement to delivery. Every commitment carries its original citation and every status change carries a dated source. Delivered late is still delivered - the dates show the journey - and when a date moves, the old one stays on the record. Nothing here is our opinion; it is the institutions' own paper, checked against time.

status_legend.delivered: The promised thing verifiably happened, even if late. The dates show how late.
status_legend.on-track: The stated timeline has not lapsed and the latest dated evidence is consistent with it.
status_legend.slipped: The institution itself has moved the date. Old and new dates are both shown.
status_legend.overdue: The promised date has passed with no delivery and no formally revised date we can cite.
status_legend.stalled: Work or approvals have stopped, by the institution's own account or a court's.
status_legend.unverified: We can cite the promise but cannot yet cite its current status either way.

commitments.title: Desilt and rejuvenate Bellandur Lake (32.33 lakh cubic metres of silt)
commitments.committed_by: Bangalore Development Authority / Government of Karnataka, under National Green Tribunal orders
commitments.what: After Bellandur caught fire in February 2017, the NGT ordered Karnataka to rejuvenate the 890-acre lake, backed by a Rs 500 crore escrow deposit and Rs 50 crore environmental compensation (order of 6 December 2018, Justice Adarsh Kumar Goel bench). BDA began desilting in December 2020 against a total of 32.33 lakh cubic metres. The completion date has moved at least five times; as of March 2026 BDA's own chief engineer put removal at 22-24 lakh cubic metres, essentially unchanged since late 2024.

commitment_source.label: NGT order of 6 Dec 2018 (India Environment Portal record); original early-2020 deadline per Deccan Herald

status_history.note: NGT accepts the Panjwani Committee's 'environmental emergency' report: Rs 500 crore to escrow for the action plan, Rs 50 crore interim compensation to CPCB, Rs 25 crore fine on BBMP, monitoring committee under Justice N. Santosh Hegde constituted.
The August 2022 desilting deadline is about to lapse; contractors tell BDA they need at least another year. The NGT's original early-2020 deadline had already been extended to 2021.
Environment Minister Eshwar Khandre sets a new target: rejuvenation complete by December 2024. About 50% of desilting done at this point; sewage inflow still ~550 MLD.

December 2024 deadline dead: BDA halted desilting in May 2024 for lack of funds. 22.69 of 32.33 lakh cubic metres removed (~70%); the Rs 500 crore escrow exhausted (Rs 250 cr STPs, Rs 100 cr Bellandur, Rs 100 cr Varthur); Rs 12 crore of invoices unpaid; wetland works only 30% done. The Hegde monitoring committee had been dissolved in 2023.
Karnataka government approves Rs 80 crore to resume desilting.
New deadline set: March 2026. BDA cites a waterlogged lakebed, slow desilting and funding delays.

The new GBA East City Corporation's commissioner D.S. Ramesh reviews both lakes and directs BDA to complete silt removal 'on priority' before the monsoon - an informal further deadline alongside the March 2026 one.

BDA chief engineer Shantha Rajanna: 'We have already removed 22 lakh to 24 lakh cubic metres' of the 32 lakh total - against 22.69 lakh already reported in December 2024. That is at most ~1.3 lakh cubic metres of movement in 14 months.

The March 2026 deadline has passed and the monsoon has set in, with no completion announcement found in any April-July 2026 coverage - checked for this register on this date. Both the formal March deadline and the commissioner's before-the-monsoon directive stand unmet on the public record.
status_history.source_label: Neer Vazhvu verification sweep, 5 Jul 2026 (no completion coverage found)

commitments.title: Desilt Varthur Lake (~15 lakh cubic metres)
commitments.committed_by: Bangalore Development Authority, under the same NGT orders as Bellandur
commitments.what: Varthur (450 acres, downstream of Bellandur) was covered by the same December 2018 NGT directions and the same slipping deadlines. Unlike Bellandur, its desilting finished - helped by farmer demand for the silt - roughly five years after the original deadline. The lake is to be handed to the Greater Bengaluru Authority's East City Corporation.

commitment_source.label: NGT order of 6 Dec 2018 (India Environment Portal record)

status_history.note: 96% of Varthur's ~15 lakh cubic metres desilted; success credited to farmers taking the silt. Bellandur lagging behind.
GBA East City Corporation commissioner D.S. Ramesh, treating Varthur's desilting as done, orders a handover report within one week at his review of both lakes.

BDA chief engineer: Varthur desilting 'completed a year ago' (i.e. ~early 2025), lake to be handed to the GBA East City Corporation. Delivered means desilting only: sewage still enters during rains, wetland development is slow, and no confirmation of the completed handover has been found.

commitments.title: Commission Cauvery Stage V (775 MLD) by March 2024
commitments.committed_by: BWSSB (Bangalore Water Supply and Sewerage Board), JICA-funded
commitments.what: Stage V adds 775 MLD from the Cauvery at Thorekadanahalli for the 110 villages added to BBMP in 2007 - the city's largest single supply addition. In December 2023 BWSSB promised completion by March 2024 and water from May 2024. It was commissioned on 16 October 2024, about five months late - a modest slip by the standards of this register.

commitment_source.label: Deccan Herald, 29 Dec 2023 (BWSSB: complete by March, trial runs April, supply from May 2024)

status_history.note: Commissioned by CM Siddaramaiah at Thorekadanahalli. JICA loan JPY 81,060 million (~Rs 4,336 crore; a later Hans India report puts the total project cost at Rs 5,550 crore - loan versus total scope). Plan: new connections across 110 villages in 8 zones, ~50 lakh beneficiaries.

commitments.title: 3 lakh new Cauvery connections 'within one month' of the Stage V launch
commitments.what: At the October 2024 launch, BWSSB set itself a target of three lakh new connections within one month (JICA's project design says four lakh). Eighteen months on, the board is at roughly 1.75 lakh connections drawing ~400 of the 775 MLD - the water exists, but half of it has no takers yet. BWSSB has tried EMI schemes and a mandatory-connection push for apartments; it has published no revised completion date we can cite.

commitment_source.label: Citizen Matters, 7 Apr 2025 ('BWSSB had set its target of an ambitious three lakh connections within one month of the launch')

status_history.note: Chairman Ram Prasath Manohar: 89,000 connections completed under Stage V. 104 of 110 villages receiving water; 6 pending on land issues; 'no clear date of completion'.

To push uptake, BWSSB launches a 12-month EMI plan for new connections (20% upfront, 80% in 12 EMIs), directed by Dy CM D.K. Shivakumar, aimed at unconnected apartments. Shivakumar had announced in February 2025 that Cauvery connections would be mandatory for apartments.
Over 1.75 lakh connections drawing ~400 MLD of the allocated 775 MLD, against the 3-lakh target - 'over 50% coverage' sixteen months after launch.

commitments.title: Cauvery Stage VI: 500 MLD more by 2028 (Rs 6,939 crore)
commitments.what: Approved by the Karnataka cabinet on 26 February 2026: another 500 MLD, taking total Cauvery supply to 2,775 MLD, for eight outskirt towns (Nelamangala, Hoskote, Devanahalli and others) plus the Kempegowda and Shivarama Karanth layouts, ~30 lakh beneficiaries. The '2028' horizon comes from the DPR-stage framing in April 2025; the cabinet-approval coverage names no completion year, and as of the approval no lender was confirmed (World Bank, JICA and HUDCO 'approached'). The clock starts now.

commitment_source.label: Deccan Herald, 26 Feb 2026 (cabinet approval); 2028 horizon per Citizen Matters, 7 Apr 2025

status_history.note: Even as Stage VI is planned, Deccan Herald reports BWSSB 'anticipated a flood, but there is only a trickle' - the board is struggling to sign up users for Stage V's water. Stage VI's case rests on demand that Stage V has not yet demonstrated.

commitments.title: Mekedatu balancing reservoir (4.75 TMC drinking water for Bengaluru)
commitments.what: A Rs 9,000 crore balancing reservoir on the Cauvery near Kanakapura: 4.75 TMC of drinking water for Bengaluru plus 400 MW of power. Karnataka submitted the DPR to the Central Water Commission on 18 January 2019 (per PIB) after CWC's in-principle nod at pre-feasibility stage. Seven years on it remains unapproved: clearance must pass through the Cauvery Water Management Authority, where Tamil Nadu has blocked it at every step. In November 2025 the Supreme Court dismissed Tamil Nadu's petitions and directed the CWMA/CWC to decide; a revised DPR went to the CWC in 2026, Tamil Nadu's CM formally asked the PM to reject it, and pre-clearance groundwork (a wildlife feasibility survey) began in mid-2026. No clearance, no bhoomi puja, no construction.

commitment_source.label: PIB (PRID 1848459): DPR submitted to CWC on 18 Jan 2019, copies forwarded to CWMA

status_history.note: The Supreme Court dismisses Tamil Nadu's petitions against the project, directing that the CWMA and CWC decide on the DPR - procedurally unblocking the file without approving anything.
status_history.source_label: SC decision Nov 2025, per Drishti IAS summary and June 2026 press references

status_history.note: Karnataka's revised DPR (drinking water only; no reduction in Tamil Nadu's share) is with the CWC; Tamil Nadu CM Vijay writes to the PM seeking its immediate rejection. Bhoomi puja deferred until CWC permission, per Dy CM D.K. Shivakumar.
status_history.source_label: India TV News, 26 May 2026; Organiser, 27 May 2026; The Federal (DPR resubmission)

status_history.note: Motion on both sides of the border, still no clearance: CM Shivakumar met the Jal Shakti minister on 12 June seeking expedited approval; the TN Assembly passed a resolution opposing the project on 19 June; and the Karnataka State Wildlife Board has conducted a feasibility survey at the site (~12,500 acres of the Cauvery Wildlife Sanctuary at stake), disclosed during a PMK protest march.
status_history.source_label: ANI, 4 Jul 2026 (wildlife survey, via PMK's Anbumani Ramadoss); Mangalorean/IANS, 12 Jun 2026 (Jal Shakti meeting)

commitments.title: K-100 'Citizens' Waterway' complete in 10 months (by ~Jan 2022)
commitments.what: The 9.6 km Koramangala valley drain from KR Market towards Bellandur, to be remade as a clean urban waterway for Rs 175 crore under the 15th Finance Commission. The foundation stone was laid on 25 March 2021 with a 10-month completion commitment. Three deadlines later it has still not been formally completed, and a May 2026 report describes the built stretches as already degrading - though sewage entering the drain has genuinely fallen from ~130 MLD to ~10 MLD, with a 5 MLD STP commissioned at Kalasipalya.

commitment_source.label: Citizen Matters, 16 Feb 2022 (foundation 25 Mar 2021, Rs 175 crore, 'over a period of 10 months')

status_history.note: January 2022 deadline missed with only ~40% of work complete; critics flag retaining walls versus NGT width orders and untouched buffer-zone encroachments.
'The third deadline': full wrap-up and inauguration promised for 15 August 2024; KR Market STP 'operational in a month'. No report confirming that inauguration happened was found.
A month past the third deadline: BBMP 'nearly completes' the makeover, but sewage flow into the drain persists. No inauguration was ever reported.

'From urban showcase to eyesore': project yet to be completed and already suffering - sewage inflow near Shantinagar, foul odour, litter, unbuilt facilities. Real gains recorded: sewage in the drain down from ~130 MLD to ~10 MLD; 5 MLD Kalasipalya STP commissioned.

commitments.title: Fill Kolar and Chikkaballapur tanks with Bengaluru's treated wastewater (KC + HN Valley)
commitments.committed_by: Minor Irrigation Department / BWSSB, Government of Karnataka
commitments.what: KC Valley (Rs 1,342 crore, inaugurated June 2018) promised 440 MLD of treated water to 126 Kolar tanks; HN Valley (Rs 970 crore) promised 210 MLD to 65 tanks in Bengaluru Rural and Chikkaballapur. Water does flow - but by October 2019 only 40 Kolar tanks had been filled, pumping was twice interrupted by courts over water quality, and in July 2025 the state's own ministers admitted the water reaching the tanks needs tertiary treatment it is not getting, with villages posting warning boards. We cannot cite a current tank-by-tank fill count.

commitment_source.label: IndiaSpend, 22 Nov 2019 (KC Valley: 440 MLD to 126 tanks, inaugurated June 2018; 40 tanks filled by Oct 2019)

status_history.note: 40 of 126 Kolar tanks filled; pumping halted by the High Court in July 2018 over quality and by a Supreme Court stay for 175 days in 2019. A September 2019 IISc report found heavy metals above standards.

Minister K.H. Muniyappa publicly admits KC/HN Valley water reaching Kolar and Chikkaballapur lakes needs tertiary treatment; CM Siddaramaiah says the project is 'meant only for groundwater recharging and not for drinking'; villages post warning boards; hyacinth reported in Kandavara, Mustoor and Kolaramma lakes. No current public tank-fill count found - hence 'unverified' rather than a firmer verdict.

commitments.title: Fill 20 (then ~30) Bengaluru city lakes with treated water
commitments.what: In April 2024 BWSSB's chairman said the board had a plan to fill 20 city lakes with treated water and had already filled 15 (Jakkur, Horamavu Agara, Doddabommasandra, Kengeri, Nagarabhavi, Yelahanka and Puttenahalli among them). By March 2025 the plan had grown to ~30 lakes, 16 of them in Mahadevapura, using treated water from apartment STPs, with pipeline tenders floated. No lake-by-lake completion register is published; we track the stated counts.

commitment_source.label: Water Digest, 18 Apr 2024 (chairman: 'plan to fill 20 lakes... already filled 15')

status_history.note: Plan expanded to ~30 lakes (16 in Mahadevapura zone) using 500-600 MLD available from apartment STPs; tenders floated for Begur Lake (Rs 1 crore) and Chikkathogur + Yelenahalli-BTM Residency (Rs 1.7 crore) pipelines.

commitments.title: Byramangala reservoir rejuvenation by 2028-29 (Rs 391 crore)
commitments.committed_by: Minor Irrigation Department / BWSSB, Government of Karnataka
commitments.what: The Karnataka cabinet cleared a Rs 391 crore plan (2025; one report says Rs 371 crore) to rejuvenate Byramangala reservoir, which receives the Vrishabhavathi's sewage-laden flow southwest of Bengaluru: desilting, plus a ~Rs 230 crore, 100 MLD BWSSB treatment plant near the lake promised 'operational within three years'. The whole project is targeted at 2028-29. A precursor GO of 23 November 2018 (Rs 110 crore diversion weir) had stalled for funds. We could not extract the exact cabinet date; the promise date below is the announcement coverage.

commitment_source.label: Newsfirst Prime (Rs 391 crore approval; Minor Irrigation Minister N.S. Boseraju; 2028-29 target)

commitments.title: Publish ward-level water consumption data on an open platform
commitments.committed_by: BWSSB, under BBMP's Bengaluru Climate Action and Resilience Plan (BCAP)
commitments.what: BCAP action W,WW,SW-1.2 (timeline: 2025) commits BWSSB to publishing ward-level data on actual consumption of piped water, by customer group, on an open-access platform, so that supply can be planned equitably. A dataset titled 'Ward wise Water consumption data' was published by BWSSB on the national Open Government Data platform on 21 June 2025 - within the promised year - and updated on 5 February 2026. Delivered means the ward-wise dataset exists in open access; the customer-group breakdown, and the follow-on promise to revisit service benchmarks using it (action 1.3), are not verified.

commitment_source.label: BCAP Sector-wise Action Recommendations (Apr 2024), water chapter p. 78, action W,WW,SW-1.2; plan launched 27 Nov 2023

status_history.note: 'Ward wise Water consumption data' published by BWSSB on data.gov.in under the National Data Sharing and Accessibility Policy; jurisdiction Bangalore Urban, sector Water and Sanitation. Last updated 5 Feb 2026 - a sign it is being maintained, not just posted once. Verified for this register on 9 Jul 2026.
status_history.source_label: Open Government Data platform, catalog 'Water consumption data' (BWSSB)

commitments.title: Cut non-revenue water to 15% by 2050
commitments.committed_by: BWSSB, under BBMP's Bengaluru Climate Action and Resilience Plan (BCAP)
commitments.what: BCAP's water track 2 sets the target: non-revenue water down to 15% by 2050. The direction so far is documented by the board itself: BWSSB chairman Ram Prasath Manohar says unaccounted-for water fell from 51% in 2013 to 26.5% in 2025, saving about 200 MLD, via district metered areas, bulk flow meters and 200 km of cast-iron pipeline replacement (3,000 km identified). Independent estimates run a few points higher (~30%). BCAP was adopted by BBMP, which has since been restructured into the Greater Bengaluru Authority's corporations; BWSSB, the responsible agency, is unchanged.

commitment_source.label: BCAP Sector-wise Action Recommendations (Apr 2024), water chapter p. 80, track W,WW,SW-2 goal; plan launched 27 Nov 2023

status_history.note: BWSSB chairman: unaccounted-for water reduced from 51% (2013) to 26.5% (2025), ~200 MLD saved. The figure is the board's own; a September 2025 academic study put losses nearer 30%. Either number leaves 11 to 15 points still to close over 24 years.
status_history.source_label: Elets eGov interview with BWSSB chairman, 27 Apr 2026

commitments.title: Reuse at least 50% of treated wastewater by 2030, 90% by 2050
commitments.committed_by: BWSSB, under BBMP's Bengaluru Climate Action and Resilience Plan (BCAP)
commitments.what: The same BCAP track 2 goal that sets the NRW target also commits the city to reusing a minimum of 50% of treated wastewater by 2030 and 90% by 2050. On the board's own April 2026 numbers - 825 MLD reused for environmental purposes plus 30 MLD for commercial applications, against roughly 1,213 MLD treated - the 2030 bar is arguably already met. The caveat is what 'environmental purposes' mostly means: pumping to Kolar and Chikkaballapur tanks, where the state's own ministers have admitted the water needs tertiary treatment it is not getting (see the KC/HN Valley entry). No independent audit of the reuse share exists.

commitment_source.label: BCAP Sector-wise Action Recommendations (Apr 2024), water chapter p. 80, track W,WW,SW-2 goal; plan launched 27 Nov 2023

status_history.note: BWSSB chairman: 825 MLD of treated water reused for environmental purposes, 30 MLD for commercial applications - about 70% of the ~1,213 MLD currently treated, though a smaller share of all sewage generated. Quality of the reused water remains the open question, per the KC/HN Valley record.
status_history.source_label: Elets eGov interview with BWSSB chairman, 27 Apr 2026

commitments.title: Make 40% of the city's surface permeable by 2040
commitments.committed_by: BBMP (now the Greater Bengaluru Authority's corporations), under BCAP
commitments.what: BCAP's water track 3 commits the city to making 40% of its surface area permeable by 2040 by reclaiming ecologically sensitive spaces and adopting nature-based solutions. BCAP's own risk assessment shows the scale of the reversal required: 63% of the city's area was already concretised by 2000, and a further 31% lost groundwater-recharge potential between 2000 and 2020. No baseline permeability figure, measurement method or progress reporting has been published, and a July 2025 review of the Climate Action Cell found sponge-space actions discussed in meetings but little documented ground progress. Unverified means exactly that: the promise is citable, its status is not.

commitment_source.label: BCAP Sector-wise Action Recommendations (Apr 2024), water chapter p. 94, track W,WW,SW-3 goal; plan launched 27 Nov 2023

status_history.note: OpenCity's review of the Climate Action Cell's first 17 months (41 meetings, Feb 2024 to Jun 2025): sponge-space restoration and aquifer mapping were discussed, but the Cell told an RTI applicant it holds no direct responsibility for monitoring outcomes, and no permeability baseline or progress metric has been published.

commitments.title: Treat 95% of the city's wastewater by 2050, about 60% of it via low-carbon systems
commitments.committed_by: BWSSB, under BBMP's Bengaluru Climate Action and Resilience Plan (BCAP)
commitments.what: BCAP's water track 4 sets the target: 95% of wastewater treated by 2050 through a mix of centralised and decentralised systems, of which about 60% should use low-carbon and nature-based technologies. As of March 2026 the city's 34 STPs (1,348.5 MLD installed) treat 1,212.7 MLD against an estimated 1,480 MLD of sewage generated - roughly 82% - with 20 plants being upgraded to NGT norms, 7 of them due by end-2026. A 2025 estimate that counts decentralised plants and a wider boundary puts generation higher (~2,140 MLD) and treatment nearer 75%; both figures are shown because the boundary definitions differ. The low-carbon 60% sub-target has no published tracking at all.

commitment_source.label: BCAP Sector-wise Action Recommendations (Apr 2024), water chapter p. 96, track W,WW,SW-4 goal; plan launched 27 Nov 2023

status_history.note: 34 STPs, 1,348.5 MLD installed capacity, 1,212.7 MLD treated against ~1,480 MLD generated (~82%); 20 STPs under NGT-norm rehabilitation (BOD 20 to 10 mg/l, tertiary stages added), 7 due by end-2026 at ~Rs 33.4 crore. BWSSB's longer roadmap projects 2,511.5 MLD across 79 plants.

update_model: Statuses change only against a dated citation. The register is re-checked against a small calendar of documents: BDA/GBA lake reviews and NGT filings for the rejuvenation entries, BWSSB announcements and Karnataka budget documents (February-March) for the Cauvery entries, CWC/CWMA agendas for Mekedatu, and for the BCAP entries the Climate Action Cell's outputs plus BCAP's own three-yearly review of targets and actions, first due around late 2026. Each commitment carries a next-check date; a passed next-check with no new citation is itself flagged, never silently updated.
sources_note: Sources are named institutions' own documents where they exist (NGT orders, JICA press releases, cabinet approvals) and dated reporting in Deccan Herald, Citizen Matters, The Hindu and others where they do not. Where two sources conflict (silt volumes, project costs, connection targets) both figures are shown with their labels. Approximate dates are marked as such.
